newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai ministry asks for 500 mln baht rice fund.
newsitem.headline: Thai ministry asks for 500 mln baht rice fund.

text.p: The Thai Commerce Ministry is seeking 500 million baht from the government to help government-to-government rice deals, ministry sources said on Monday.
The request was scheduled to be considered by the Rice Policy Committee in its meeting later Monday, they added.
The fund will be used to compensate for losses incurred from government-to-government rice deals. If approved, the fund will be used from November 1996 to December 1997.

"The new crop will enter the market in November. We will use this money to absorb some supply during that time to support prices," one official said. "The money will be used to cover losses from rice purchases, foreign exchange losses and others."

Ministry sources said the fund was based on a government-to-government export target of one million tonnes -- 400,000 tonnes to Iran, 200,000 tonnes of the Philippines, another 200,000 to Indonesia, 100,000 tonnes to China, 25,000 to Brunei and the rest to European and African countries.

"We encourage the private sector to export as much as possible. But the government will have to sell directly to certain markets because we need to keep those markets," another ministry official said.
